title: Search Usernames Across Platforms: Review & Action
description: Run a public username sweep, review source URLs, confirm your own old accounts and turn candidate results into verified account actions.
h1: Search Usernames Across Platforms: Review & Action
intro: A public username sweep is useful for finding candidate profiles under a handle you have used. It is less useful for proving ownership or checking whether a name can be registered. This workflow combines MyRecon results with original-page checks and your own account records.

sections.heading: Prepare handles and a private account log
sections.body: List the exact handles you remember using and note which services you already know. Search each spelling separately rather than assuming punctuation, capitalization or suffixes are interchangeable on every platform. Keep the inventory private. Your password manager and old signup emails can find accounts that public discovery misses; do not upload a password-manager export or use a personal password as a search term.

sections.heading: Choose the scope you actually need
sections.body: Start with a standard MyRecon sweep. The release catalogue covers 500+ platforms. Guests receive a limited preview; signed-in free accounts get five complete standard scans per day. Paid plans add features and a separate Extended catalogue; the current pricing page gives the available checkout and limits. An attempted platform count is not a count of confirmed accounts. A broader scan may add unavailable checks and more candidates to review.

sections.heading: Review statuses and original URLs
sections.body: Keep found, not found and unknown separate. Open reported candidates at their original service. Confirm that the page is a profile for the requested handle rather than a generic login page or redirected home page. If access is blocked, record unable to verify. MyRecon does not directly check Discord; use the manual Discord guide for accounts you already interact with. Do not interpret a similarly named profile on another service as proof of a Discord account.

sections.heading: Confirm ownership using your own records
sections.body: For a self-audit, compare each candidate with a saved login, signup email or a known account link you published. Do not trigger password recovery for someone else to test account existence. If you lack ownership evidence, label the candidate unresolved. For an authorized organizational review, use the official account register and source-controlled links; a shared handle alone cannot establish identity.

sections.heading: Worked example: three outcomes
sections.body: Illustrative case: a former handle returns a recognized GitHub profile, an Instagram login wall and a missing-page response on a forum. The GitHub result is a candidate until your records confirm it. The Instagram view is unavailable under the observed access context. The forum result is a dated negative for that handle, not proof that you never had a forum account under another name. Record each result separately rather than writing no online footprint.

sections.heading: Finish with account actions and a recheck
sections.body: For confirmed accounts, choose keep and secure, reduce public visibility or close through official settings. Export material you want before deletion and review connected application permissions. Reopen the public URL after the change to verify what a visitor can see. Save a short action log and delete unnecessary screenshots. To choose an unused brand handle, use the official registration flow instead of a profile-presence result; reserved and suspended names can remain unavailable.

cta.label: Search a public username with MyRecon

faq.question: Can I use a sweep to register an available username?
faq.answer: A not-found result does not guarantee registration availability. Check the platform's official signup or handle-change flow.

faq.question: Should I combine different spellings into one identity?
faq.answer: No. Search separately and confirm ownership with independent evidence or your own records.

faq.question: What should I do after finding an old account?
faq.answer: Confirm ownership, review recovery and public fields, then secure or close the account through its official service.

takeaways: Prepare handles and a private account log
Choose the scope you actually need
method: Worked examples are illustrative unless explicitly labeled as observed. Product limits were checked against the release source; linked provider instructions describe external workflows, not a claim that every account flow was tested.
